name: Sunstone
physical: Linked to a warm, energized feeling
Kept nearby for stamina during busy days
summary: Sunstone is the sparkling orange feldspar of joy and vitality, famous for the glittering copper flakes that light it up from within in crystal lore.
intro: Sunstone is a feldspar that seems to carry sunlight inside it. Tiny flat crystals of copper or hematite are trapped within the stone, and when light hits them they flash like scattered sparks, an effect called aventurescence. Colors range from pale champagne to rich orange, rose, and red, and the most prized Oregon stones can even show green or blue. Sunstone is found in Oregon in the United States, in India, in Tanzania, and in Norway, among other places. It is cut into cabochons, beads, and faceted gems, and is also the official state gem of Oregon. People adore it because it looks warm, glittery, and cheerful.
history: Sunstone is one of the oldest named gems in the Mediterranean world. Ancient writers spoke of a stone that shimmered like the Sun, and some scholars think the Vikings may have used a Norwegian sunstone, possibly a polarizing crystal, to find the Sun on cloudy days, though this remains speculation. Native Americans in what is now Oregon knew the sparkling feldspar for centuries and used it in trade and ceremony. Commercial mining began in the nineteenth century, and Oregon sunstone was named the state gem in 1987. In older lore, sunstone was carried as a charm for good fortune and as a symbol of the solar deities.
meaning: In the crystal tradition sunstone is a stone of sunshine. Practitioners link it to the Sacral and Solar Plexus chakras, associating it with vitality, personal power, and joy. It is said to lift the spirits when the days are dark and to encourage generosity and leadership. Many people keep it close for confidence before presentations, interviews, or new projects. Its flash of copper is traditionally tied to abundance and good luck. Because it is a fire and Sun stone, it is also used to energize creative work and to add warmth to relationships. It is often recommended for people who feel run down by winter, as a reminder to seek light and joy. Those who feel overwhelmed may want to use it in moderation, as its energy is lively.
howToUse: Wear sunstone as a ring, bracelet, or pendant to start your day with a bright intention. Place a piece on your desk or in a sunny window for a mood lift. Hold a palm stone during morning meditation, visualizing the Sun rising in your belly. In a prosperity grid, use it with citrine and pyrite. Place it near your workspace when starting creative projects, or carry a tumbled stone when you need courage to speak up. Some people keep a piece in the car or bag as a travel charm for cheerful journeys.
care: Sunstone is Mohs 6 to 6.5 with two cleavage directions, so it can chip. A short rinse in lukewarm water is fine, but dry it right away and avoid ultrasonic cleaners or steam. It is stable in sunlight and loves a sunny windowsill, which makes sunbathing the classic way to cleanse and charge it. Sound and smoke also work. Store it apart from harder gems to prevent scratches.
identify: Natural sunstone shows tiny glittering flakes that appear and disappear as you rotate the stone. Beware of goldstone, a man-made glass with copper crystals that looks similar but is uniformly sparkly with no feldspar structure. Some Oregon green and red sunstones are copper-diffused, which means the color was added by treatment, and should be disclosed. Orange glass or dyed feldspar may lack any true aventurescence.

faq.a: Sunstone is traditionally linked with vitality, optimism, leadership, and abundance. Many people use it to lift their mood, build confidence, and bring a sense of warmth into their day, especially when light is scarce.

faq.q: Is sunstone the same as goldstone?
faq.a: No. Sunstone is a natural feldspar with tiny copper or hematite flakes. Goldstone is man-made glass with copper crystals added. Goldstone is more uniformly sparkly, while sunstone shows flashes that shift as you tilt it.

faq.q: Can sunstone go in the sun?
faq.a: Yes, sunstone is stable in sunlight, and a sunny sill is the classic way to charge it. Avoid long soaks in water or ultrasonic cleaners because the stone has cleavage and can chip with hard knocks.
